title: Remove Linked List Elements
prompt:
Given the `head` of a singly linked list and an integer `val`, remove all nodes whose value equals `val` and return the new head.

The list is given as an array (e.g. `[1,2,6,3,4,5,6]` represents `1 -> 2 -> 6 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 6 -> null`). The starter code includes helpers to convert between the array and a linked-list node — build the actual list, unlink the matching nodes by manipulating `next` pointers, then convert back to an array to return.
constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [0, 10^4]
hints: The tricky part is removing nodes at the very front of the list, since that changes what head is.
Use a dummy node pointing to head so every removal — including at the front — is handled the same way.
Walk a pointer through the list; whenever the next node's value matches val, skip over it by relinking next instead of advancing.

solution.approach: Use a dummy node before head so that removing the first node requires no special case. Walk a pointer `curr` starting at dummy; while curr.next exists, if curr.next.val equals val, splice it out with curr.next = curr.next.next (without advancing curr, since the new curr.next also needs checking), otherwise advance curr. Return dummy.next.
